title: CLR/29/2013 of URBAN COOPERATIVE BANK LIMITED Vs RAM KUMAR AGARWAL

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No. 29 of 2013
Urban Cooperative Bank Ltd. ....... Revisionist
 versus
Ram Kumar Agarwal ....... Respondent
Mr. Gopal K. Verma, Advocate for the defendant / revisionist.
None present for the respondent despite service of notice.
U.C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)

By means of present civil revision, the
defendant / revisionist seeks to set aside the impugned
order dated 16.01.2013, passed by learned Addl.
District Judge, Dehradun in Misc. Case no. 33 of 2011
(First Appeal no. 39 of 1988), whereby said Court has
dismissed the application under Section 5 of the
Limitation Act alongwith restoration application filed
by the defendant / revisionist.
2) The main grounds which have been taken
by the revisionist in the present civil revision while
challenging the impugned order are being reproduced
here-in-below for convenience:
 (1) That the opposite party took a loan from the
respondent bank, but when he did not repay the
amount of loan, then as per the provision of the Co-operative Society Act, the revisionist obtained a
decree of Rs. 96,319.57 plus interest against the

2
opposite party. Pursuant to said decree a recovery
certificate was issued against the opposite party for
recovery of amount of Rs. 1,05,012.37 plus interest.
 (2) That against the said decree, the
revisionist filed a suit no. 348 of 1984 (Ram Kumar
Aggarwal vs The Urban Cooperative Bank Ltd.) for
permanent injunction against the recovery of the
amount in the court of Civil Judge, Dehradun.
 (3) That the revisionist filed its written
statement before the court below whereby denying
averment of the plaint.
 (4) That the court below vide order dated
26.09.1988, decreed the suit of the plaintiff / opposite
party.
 (5) That feeling aggrieved by the judgment
and decree passed by Civil Judge, Dehradun, the
revisionist filed a first appeal no. 39 of 1988 before
Hon'ble Allahabad High Court.
 (6) That in the year 1995, the State
Government of Uttar Pradesh made an amendment in
sub-section 1(1A)(1B) of Section 21 of Bengal, Agra,
Assam Civil Court Act, 1887, as amended vide U.P.
Civil Lodge Amendment Act, 1991. The High Court
of Allahabad in view of the Notification no. 211/IV-G-27-06, May 1995, transferred the said first appeal
no. 39 of 1988 to District Judge, Dehradun for
adjudication.
 (7) That it is pertinent to mention here that
after the transfer of the appeal from Allahabad High
Court, the revisionist bank appointed Sri Shushul

3
Kumar Angre, Advocate to pursue the matter before
the court below. Unfortunately the counsel for the
revisionist died on 31.03.2006.
 (8) That on 03.08.2006, Addl. District Judge
/ 7 F.T.C., Dehradun passed an order whereby said
court dismissed the first appeal for non-prosecution
of the revisionist.
 (9) That when the revisionist came to know
about the dismissal of the first appeal, the revisionist
contacted another counsel Sri Vijay Kumar Gupta,
Advocate to know about the first appeal before the
court below. The counsel of revisionist on
12.09.2008 inspected the records of the first appeal
then it was revealed that the said appeal was
dismissed for non-prosecution. Mentioning all these
facts, the revisionist filed a restoration application
before the court below.
 (10) That the said restoration application
remained pending before the court below for kind
consideration and unfortunately on 23.07.2010, the
counsel of revisionist due to some personal un-avoidable reasons could not attend the court and, the
court below vide order dated 23.07.2010, passed an
order dismissing the restoration application of the
revisionist.
 (11) That again on 23.05.2011, the revisionist
filed an application under Order 9 Rule 4 read with
151 C.P.C. for restoration of the earlier orders dated
23.07.2010 as well as 03.08.2006 alongwith an

4
application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for
condonation of delay in filing restoration application.
 (12) That by the impugned order dated
16.01.2013, the court below without considering the
facts and circumstances narrated in the restoration
application and delay condonation application,
dismissed the application for condonation of delay
and send the file to record room.
 (13) That the court below instead of passing
orders on restoration application of the revisionist
bank, rejected the application for condonation of
delay without assigning any valid and justified
reason.
3) The court below has observed in the
impugned order that the first appeal filed by the
appellant (revisionist herein) was dismissed on
03.08.2006 in his absence. He moved a restoration
application for restoring the First appeal, which was
also dismissed by learned Addl. District Judge / F.T.C.
II, Dehradun on 23.07.2010. The First Appeal was
received in the Court of Addl. District Judge / F.T.C. II
on 26.09.2008, which remained vacant from 16.10.2009
to 30.04.2010, but the restoration application was
dismissed on 23.07.2010, in as much as, none appeared
for the appellant before said Court on the date fixed.
Learned court below was of the opinion that the
appellant cannot be given any benefit of the mistake
committed by his counsel. There was ten month's

5
delay in filing the restoration application and no reason
has been assigned for such delay. The court below,
therefore, did not think it proper to allow the
application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
Feeling aggrieved against the same, present civil
revision has been filed on behalf of the revisionist.
4) Notice was issued to the respondent through
dasti as well as by registered post. An affidavit of
service has been filed on behalf of the revisionist to
indicate that the notice was served upon the respondent.
Registry has indicated the same in its report dated
07.05.2013. The civil revision was taken up by this
Court on 03.06.2015, 04.06.2015 and 18.06.2015, but
none appeared for the respondent even in the revised
call despite service of notice. The Court has, therefore,
no option but to decide the civil revision in the absence
of respondent.

5) The circumstances as has been narrated on
behalf of the revisionist in the grounds of revision as
also the facts which have been indicated by the court
below in its order under challenge, suggest that the
revisionist's application under Section 5 of the
Limitation Act ought to have been allowed and the
restoration application ought to have been heard on
merits. Heaven would not have fallen had such
opportunity granted to the revisionist. The facts are
clear that the restoration application was filed in a court

6
which remained vacant from 16.10.2009 to 30.04.2010.
Normally learned counsel do not seriously appear in a
vacant court and, therefore, the mistake, if any,
committed by learned counsel for the revisionist in the
court below was pardonable. It was for the court below
to have considered ten month's delay in filing the
restoration application in the context of peculiar facts
and circumstances of the case, a detailed reference of
which has already been given in the foregoing
paragraphs of the judgment.
6) Civil Revision is, therefore, allowed. Order
impugned is set aside. The matter is remitted back to
the court below to consider the application under
Section 5 of the Limitation Act filed on behalf of the
revisionist, as per law, after granting opportunity of
hearing to both the sides. Since the matter pertains to
the year 1984, therefore, learned court below is
requested to make an endeavour to decide such
application at the earliest possible, in accordance with
law.
